## Idea

Instead of choosing one resolution in `FindClusters()`, `coclustR` clusters
the cells with every combination of number of PCs, number of neighbours and
resolution, and builds a consensus from how often each pair of cells falls
in the same cluster. Each step is explained in detail in
`vignette("coclustR-sce")`; here we focus on the Seurat workflow.

```{r libs}
library(coclustR)
library(Seurat)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Simulated data and standard Seurat pipeline

`simulate_sc_counts()` generates five known populations: `Pop1` and `Pop2`
are similar (they share markers) and `Pop5` is a rare, very distinct cell
type (60 cells).

```{r simulate}
sim <- simulate_sc_counts(n_cells = c(400, 300, 250, 150, 60), seed = 1)
seu <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = sim$counts, meta.data = sim$cell_data)
seu
```

```{r preprocess}
seu <- NormalizeData(seu, verbose = FALSE)
seu <- FindVariableFeatures(seu, verbose = FALSE)
seu <- ScaleData(seu, verbose = FALSE)
seu <- RunPCA(seu, npcs = 30, verbose = FALSE)
seu <- RunUMAP(seu, dims = 1:30, verbose = FALSE)
DimPlot(seu, group.by = "population")
```

## Reference: a single `FindClusters()`

For comparison, the usual Seurat clustering at two resolutions:

```{r seurat-clusters}
seu <- FindNeighbors(seu, dims = 1:30, verbose = FALSE)
seu <- FindClusters(seu, resolution = c(0.3, 1.2), verbose = FALSE)
table(population = seu$population, res0.3 = seu$RNA_snn_res.0.3)
table(population = seu$population, res1.2 = seu$RNA_snn_res.1.2)
```

The result depends on the resolution; the consensus avoids having to pick
one.

## Consensus co-clustering

The package never changes the **future** plan; to run in parallel:

```{r plan, eval = FALSE}
future::plan(future::multisession, workers = 4)
options(future.globals.maxSize = 6 * 1024^3)
```

Here we run sequentially with a reduced grid (54 runs):

```{r grid}
future::plan(future::sequential)

grid <- run_clustering_grid(
  seu,
  reduction   = "pca",          # name of the reduction in Seurat
  n_dims      = c(10, 20, 30),
  k           = c(10, 20, 30),
  resolutions = seq(0.2, 1.2, 0.2),
  seed        = 11,
  verbose     = FALSE
)
grid
```

> Note: the `k` of `bluster::makeSNNGraph()` does not count the cell itself,
> unlike `k.param` in `FindNeighbors()`: `k = 20` is roughly equivalent to
> `k.param = 21`. The pruning (`prune = 1/15`) is the same as Seurat's
> `prune.SNN`.

```{r grid-plots, fig.height = 4}
plot_grid_overview(grid)
plot_grid_metrics(grid, metrics = c("modularity", "n_clusters"))
```

Consensus with the default parameters (complete linkage,
`min_cluster_size = 50`). The labels are added to `seu@meta.data` and the
full result is stored in `seu@misc$coclustR`:

```{r consensus}
seu <- run_coclustering(seu, grid = grid)
get_coclust_result(seu)
head(seu[[c("population", "coclust_Hybrid", "coclust_DynamicTree")]])
```

```{r compare}
table(population = seu$population, Hybrid = seu$coclust_Hybrid)
```

`Pop3`, `Pop4` and the rare population `Pop5` are recovered well, but with
*complete linkage* `Pop1` and `Pop2` (which share markers) end up in the
same cluster. This is not a failure of the consensus: in the Seurat PCA
(noisier than the one in the SingleCellExperiment vignette) many runs of
the grid mix or split these two populations in different ways, so their
meta-barcodes co-cluster at intermediate frequencies. `DynamicTree`, being
more conservative, leaves many of those cells as `Unstable`:

```{r compare-dyn}
table(population = seu$population, DynamicTree = seu$coclust_DynamicTree)
```

### Trying another linkage without re-running the grid

The consensus takes seconds, so it can be explored. With *average linkage*
(which uses the mean co-clustering between groups instead of the minimum)
`Pop1` and `Pop2` are separated. We store the result with another prefix to
keep both:

```{r average}
seu <- run_coclustering(seu, grid = grid, linkage = "average",
                        prefix = "coclustAvg_", verbose = FALSE)
table(population = seu$population, Hybrid_avg = seu$coclustAvg_Hybrid)
```

ARI against the simulated populations: consensus vs the two
`FindClusters()` resolutions and vs the median of the grid runs.

```{r ari}
ari <- function(x) bluster::pairwiseRand(seu$population, x, mode = "index")
round(c(FindClusters_res0.3 = ari(seu$RNA_snn_res.0.3),
        FindClusters_res1.2 = ari(seu$RNA_snn_res.1.2),
        grid_median         = median(apply(grid$labels, 2, ari)),
        Hybrid_complete     = ari(seu$coclust_Hybrid),
        Hybrid_average      = ari(seu$coclustAvg_Hybrid)), 3)
```

Real data have no ground truth to compare with: look at the co-clustering
heatmap (below) and at the marker genes to decide whether a split is
biological.

## Visualisation

The new columns are regular Seurat metadata, so `DimPlot()` works
directly:

```{r dimplot, fig.height = 4}
DimPlot(seu, group.by = c("coclust_Hybrid", "coclustAvg_Hybrid", "population"),
        label = TRUE)
```

The `coclustR` functions accept Seurat objects just like
SingleCellExperiment objects (by default they use the `"umap"` reduction).
Those that use the stored result (`plot_stability()`,
`plot_coclustering_heatmap()`) show the one from the last call to
`run_coclustering()`, here the *average linkage* one:

```{r coclust-plots, fig.height = 4}
plot_clusters_embedding(seu, color_by = c("coclustAvg_Hybrid",
                                          "coclustAvg_DynamicTree"))
plot_stability(seu)
```

```{r heatmap, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 7}
plot_coclustering_heatmap(seu, n_cells = 500,
                          stratify_by = c("Sample", "Hybrid"),
                          annotate_by = c("Sample", "population"))
```

## Markers of the consensus clusters

`Unstable` cells can be excluded before differential expression:

```{r markers}
Idents(seu) <- "coclustAvg_Hybrid"
seu_stable <- subset(seu, idents = "Unstable", invert = TRUE)
markers <- FindAllMarkers(seu_stable, only.pos = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
head(markers[order(markers$cluster, markers$p_val_adj), ], 10)
```

## Re-running only the consensus

`coclust_from_grid()` reuses the grid and returns the result without
modifying the object. For example, without the rescue of stable
populations, the most reproducible populations, which collapse into one or
a few meta-barcodes, are lost (`Unstable`) or merged into another cluster
by the PAM step of Hybrid:

```{r no-rescue}
no_rescue <- coclust_from_grid(grid, linkage = "average",
                               rescue_min_cells = NULL, verbose = FALSE)
table(population = seu$population, Hybrid = no_rescue$cell_clusters$Hybrid)
```

## Using an integrated embedding

If you integrated samples (Harmony, CCA, ...), just pass the corresponding
reduction, e.g. `run_coclustering(seu, reduction = "harmony")`. A
cells × dimensions matrix can also be passed directly:

```{r matrix, eval = FALSE}
res <- run_coclustering(Embeddings(seu, "pca"), n_dims = c(10, 20, 30))
```
